niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a Jungian psychology approach, a broader spiritual framework, or a regular contemplative practice. Based on the available course information, these are good starting points:

| Course | Best for | What it offers |
|---|---|---|
| **Jung Platform — Shadow courses** | A structured, Jungian introduction | A learning path covering personal and collective shadow, projection, relationships, dreams, and practical reflection. Includes material from several teachers, including Jungian analyst James Hollis. [Browse the courses](https://jungplatform.com/program/shadow-courses) |
| **Jung Platform — Engage the Shadow** | Multiple perspectives and practical tools | An eight-hour, ten-class course with ten depth-psychology speakers. Topics include shadow in relationships, dreams, and collective life. [Course page](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow) |
| **Jungian Center for the Spiritual Sciences — Shadow Work** | A lower-cost, self-paced option | Four audio lectures with written materials, exercises, and readings. Listed at $75 in the available course information. [Course listing](https://jungian.directory/courses/shadow-work/) |
| **Charlie Morley — Embracing the Shadow** | A blend of Buddhist practice and psychology | A self-paced, seven-week course drawing on Tibetan Buddhist methods, mindfulness, insight training, and Western psychology. [Course page](https://www.charliemorley.com/shadow-work) |
| **Contemplative Studies at CTS — Contemplative Living I** | Building a sustained spiritual practice | A four-month online Christian contemplative course with personal practice, group meetings, a weekly prayer chapel, and listening circles. It’s tradition-specific, so it’s a fit if that orientation appeals to you. [Course page](https://ctsnet.edu/events/contemplative-living-i-contemplative-practices-in-daily-life/) |

**My short recommendation:** Start with **Jung Platform’s shadow pathway** if you want a thoughtful, psychology-centered introduction. Choose **Charlie Morley** if you want shadow work explicitly paired with meditation and Buddhist practice. For a regular spiritual routine rather than shadow work specifically, consider **Contemplative Living I** if Christian contemplative practice suits you.

A note of care: shadow work can bring up painful memories or intense emotions. Prefer courses that encourage pacing, boundaries, and support rather than promising a quick “healing” or transformation. A course is educational, not a substitute for therapy; if the work feels destabilizing, pause and consider working with a qualified mental-health professional. Course schedules and prices can change, so check the provider’s current page before enrolling.
